input.evidence: deploy.yml contains hardcoded AWS secret access key, database password, and Slack webhook; release.yml contains hardcoded PyPI API token and Docker Hub token.
input.recommendation: Remove hardcoded secrets from workflow files and use GitHub Actions Secrets (e.g. ${{ secrets.AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }}) instead.
input.description: Hardcoded secrets in GitHub Actions workflow environment variables

input.recommendation: Use pull_request_target carefully or restrict pull_request triggers so that untrusted PRs cannot execute build/publish steps or exfiltrate secrets.
input.description: CI workflow triggered on pull_request performs builds, test publications, and secret exposure steps without security hardening
input.evidence: ci.yml triggers on pull_request from fork/branches, prints secrets, runs npm publish, and uploads sensitive files.

input.recommendation: Remove debug logging steps that print or echo secrets and tokens.
input.evidence: ci.yml prints secrets and printsenv; deploy.yml echoes AWS access key with set -x enabled; release.yml echoes tokens and credentials in debug steps.
input.description: Exposing sensitive environment variables and secrets via debug logs and shell commands

input.evidence: ci.yml uploads .env, .env.production, and credentials.json as artifacts; release.yml uploads ~/.ssh/id_rsa, private-key.pem, and .env.local.
input.description: Uploading sensitive files and private keys as workflow artifacts
input.recommendation: Ensure artifact paths do not include sensitive config files, credential files, or private keys.

input.evidence: All workflows use action references pinned only to major versions (e.g. actions/checkout@v4, actions/setup-node@v4, actions/upload-artifact@v4) rather than immutable commit SHAs.
input.recommendation: Pin third-party actions to immutable commit SHAs with version tags as comments for supply chain security.
input.description: Unpinned third-party GitHub Actions without commit SHA pinning

input.summary: Audited the repository's GitHub Actions workflows and identified critical security and CI/CD violations including hardcoded production secrets in workflow files, untrusted pull_request triggers running publishing logic, secret exfiltration in debug/printenv steps, uploading sensitive files and private keys as workflow artifacts, and using unpinned third-party action versions.
